question: A charity communications officer is preparing a Claude-assisted case study about a named service user for the charity's public annual review. In which order should these steps be taken?
options: A) Publish it and keep a note of what was checked; confirm that the service user consents to her story being published; confirm that the draft says nothing about her that the case records do not support; state in the piece that Claude helped write it.

B) Confirm that the draft says nothing about her that the case records do not support; confirm that the service user consents to her story being published; state in the piece that Claude helped write it; publish it and keep a note of what was checked.

C) Confirm that the service user consents to her story being published; confirm that the draft says nothing about her that the case records do not support; state in the piece that Claude helped write it; publish it and keep a note of what was checked.

D) State in the piece that Claude helped write it; confirm that the draft says nothing about her that the case records do not support; confirm that the service user consents to her story being published; publish it and keep a note of what was checked.
correct_answers: C) Confirm that the service user consents to her story being published; confirm that the draft says nothing about her that the case records do not support; state in the piece that Claude helped write it; publish it and keep a note of what was checked.
explanations: The case study goes public before consent, accuracy and disclosure have been dealt with, so every safeguard is applied to something the service user has already been exposed by.
Effort goes into verifying a story the subject may not have agreed to tell, and consent is sought only after the charity has already worked her personal circumstances into a publishable draft.

Correct. Consent from the person whose story it is comes first, because without it the piece should not exist; the draft is then checked against the records so that nothing invented is attributed to her; the disclosure of AI assistance is added before publication rather than after; and the record of what was checked makes the whole thing accountable later.
The disclosure is settled first, which is the least urgent of the four, while the two questions that protect the service user are left until later in the sequence.
